chunks: If I speak, they will say: He is greedy for power,
and if I remain silent, they will say: He is grieving from death!
Far off is that, after the ups and downs!
By Allah, the son of Abu Talib is more familiar with death than an infant with the breast of its mother,
Rather, I have merged with the hidden reservoir of knowledge; if I were to disclose it, you would tremble with the trembling of the ropes in deep wells!

key_terms.ابْنُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ: son of Abu Talib (referring to Imam Ali)
key_terms.الْأَرِْيَةِ: ropes (used in drawing water from deep wells)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about his knowledge and death in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage, often cited in discussions of the 'Dilemma of Silence' (Khuruj al-Samt), highlights Imam Ali's strategic patience during the caliphate period, where he concealed his right to leadership to preserve the unity of Islam. The metaphor of the child with the mother's milk emphasizes his innate, natural affinity for death and martyrdom, contrasting with the political maneuvering of his rivals. His reference to 'hidden knowledge' (Maknun 'Ilm) alludes to the esoteric depths of the Quran and prophetic traditions that, if fully disclosed, would overwhelm the people, a concept central to Shia theological understanding of the Imam's unique spiritual authority.

en.sayed-ali-raza: If I speak out they would call me greedy towards power
but if I keep quiet they would say I was afraid of death.
It is a pity that after all the ups and downs (I have been through).
By Allāh the son of Abu Ṭalib [2] is more familiar with death than an infant with the breast of its mother.
I have hidden knowledge; if I disclose it you will start trembling like ropes in deep wells.
